title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
summary: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.

title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
summary: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

title: A Local Fourier-Transform Proof of Offen's Spherical Transfer Theorem
summary: Let $E/F$ be an unramified quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero and odd residual characteristic. Offen proved that, on the full spherical space of nondegenerate Hermitian matrices, equality of the Hironaka and Satake transforms implies Jacquet--Ye matching. We give a purely local proof of this theorem. The argument combines Jacquet's compatibility of matching with Fourier transform, the Godement--Jacquet functional equation, and Hironaka's scalar functional equation for Hermitian zeta integrals. The local proof recovers Jacquet's spherical-Hecke fundamental lemma from the unit case.

title: Erdős--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
summary: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erdős--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.

title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
summary: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

title: Clusters of primes revisited
summary: We revisit the generalized Rayleigh quotient optimization problem related to the Maynard-Tao sieve with the goal of finding a more efficient function basis. We demonstrate that a family based on products of reciprocals, previously used in asymptotic estimates for $H_m = \liminf_{n \to \infty}(p_{n+m}-p_n)$, provides results that are close to the theoretical limits of the sieve across many regimes. In particular, we establish $H_2 \leq 31 \, 140$, $H_3 \leq 2 \, 560 \, 022$, $H_4 \leq 193 \, 672 \, 056$, and $H_5 \leq 13 \, 659 \, 045 \, 840$. We also show that, as $k \to \infty$, the related variational quantity $M_k$, introduced by Maynard, satisfies the lower bound $M_k \geq \log k - 0.273572 + o(1)$.

title: Composition factor algebras and finite representation type
summary: An Artin algebra is called a composition factor algebra if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. We prove that every composition factor algebra is representation-finite. This settles a conjecture of Auslander, Reiten and Smalø. We also give criteria for comma categories and factorization categories to be of finite representation type.

title: A spectral theory of zeta functions of function fields
summary: We study Hilbert spaces constructed from the Weil quadratic form associated with the zeta function of a curve over a finite field, together with self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator on these spaces. For a distinguished family of these extensions, we prove that the eigenvalues converge to the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function and that the corresponding entire spectral functions, after normalization, converge locally uniformly to an infinite product determined by these zeros. These limits occur as the interval parameter approaches a finite endpoint, rather than infinity as in the setting of the Riemann zeta function. We also realize the global Hilbert space through the Rosati trace pairing and show that translation by $\log q$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by normalized Frobenius. This provides a geometric model for the analogous analytic constructions associated with the Riemann zeta function.

title: Push forwards of smooth measures on the unitary group in odd characteristic under the Chevalley map are almost bounded
summary:
In this paper we study analytic properties of the Chevalley map $p:\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{c}$ where $\mathfrak{u}$ is the Lie algebra of a unitary group over a local field of odd characteristics. This map essentially sends a matrix to its characteristic polynomial.
  Our main result is that smooth compactly supported measures on $\mathfrak{u}$ are pushed by the Chevalley map to measures on $\mathfrak{c}$ with density functions in $L^q(\mathfrak{c})$ for all $q < \infty$. We also provide similar results for the Chevalley map attached to the unitary group.
  An important consequence is an odd characteristic analogue to results of Harish-Chandra stating the local integrability of the orbital integrals on the unitary group and its Lie algebra. Further possible applications to local integrability of characters of admissible representations of unitary groups over local fields of odd characteristic are also discussed.

title: Weil Operators and Remainders of Anderson Generating Functions over a Punctured Projective Line
summary: Let $A_ρ$ be the coordinate ring of the projective line over $\Fq$ with a closed point of degree $N$ removed. We give finite formulas for higher Weil operators in a basis of Riemann--Roch spaces, which recover the formulas of Hu--Ou--Yang when $N=1$. We identifythese operators with representatives of the residue Casimir tensors and obtain a determinant formula for the Weil pairing, relative to a chosen determinant realization. For a normalized rank-one Drinfeld module, we compute the remainder of its Anderson generating function modulo any nonconstant $p\in A_ρ$. The formula includes multiple zeros and a zero at the ordinary point at infinity. Its last coefficient is a nonzero scalar multiple of an exponential division value. When $(p)$ is a finite principal prime, a value of the associated special function at one zero of $p$ generates the torsion field after adjoining that zero. We give an explicit $q$-linear formula recovering a torsion generator from this value. We also specialize the evaluation theorem of Gazda--Maurischat and compute the different as the principal ideal $(\partial_xp)$.

title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
summary: We classify the connected components of support $τ$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $τ$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $τ$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $τ$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $τ$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.

title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant Γ_{1,4} = 8
summary: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants Γ_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

title: A note on rational wavefront sets for finite special orthogonal groups
summary: We study rational wavefront sets of irreducible representations of finite special orthogonal groups over $\mathbb F_q$. We assume that $q$ is odd and that both $q$ and its characteristic are sufficiently large. Using {the second author's} results for full orthogonal groups, we determine the maximal rational wavefront sets and the dimensions of the corresponding generalized Whittaker models. We show that each rational wavefront set is the rational closure of its maximal elements. For unipotent representations, we describe the maximal rational wavefront sets in terms of Lusztig's canonical quotient and their behavior under Alvis--Curtis duality.

title: Vector Valued Katok-Sarnak Formulas
summary: We introduce a version of the Katok-Sarnak formula linking twisted traces of scalar valued Maass cusp forms for $Γ_0(N)$ with $N$ square-free to Fourier coefficients of vector valued Maass cusp forms for the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and the Weil representation associated to a lattice of signature $(2,1)$. We prove this by computing the Fourier coefficients of the vector valued Siegel and Millson theta lift of a scalar valued newform by two different methods and comparing the results.

title: On unitary representations of $p$-adic $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ of purely bad parity
summary: Let $G$ be $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$ or split $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$ over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We classify the irreducible unitary representations of $G$ of purely bad parity: such a representation is unitary if and only if it is of Arthur type, except for one additional family when $G=\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$. In particular, we confirm the remaining case of Ciubotaru's conjecture for $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$, namely that every unitary unipotent representation with integral infinitesimal parameter is of Arthur type.

title: Kloosterman Sums and Plücker Height Zeta Functions
summary: We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.

title: Derived tame monomial algebras
summary: We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.

title: Primes and the Möbius function over quadratic polynomials
summary: We prove an asymptotic formula for the number of primes $p\leq X$ of the form $n^2+h$ for almost all $h \leq X^{1/2-o(1)}$. We prove that, for almost all $h \leq X^{2/5}$, the number of primes satisfies a correct-order lower bound. We also show cancellation of the Möbius function over $n^2+h$ for almost all $h < X^{1/2-o(1)}$.

title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
summary: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $π$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $π$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence.

title: Twisted second moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions with applications to weighted one-level density
summary: We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.

title: Decomposing super unitary representations using Berezin integration
summary: I introduce the notion of a family of super unitary representations depending upon odd parameters as well as the notion of a direct Berezin integral of such representations. I use this to decompose the (left-)regular representation of the super Heisenberg group and of a super Heisenberg-like group into smaller (irreducible) subrepresentations. I compare the obtained subrepresentations to the representations obtained by applying (super) geometric quantization of the coadjoint orbits of the corresponding groups. It turns out that for the super Heisenberg group we need coadjoint orbits with an odd symplectic form in order to describe all subrepresentations found in the decomposition and for the Heisenberg-like super group we even need orbits with a non-homogeneous symplectic form.

title: Irrationality of values of $L$-functions for real Dirichlet characters
summary: Let $χ$ be a non-trivial real Dirichlet character and $s$ be a sufficiently large integer. In this paper, we prove that among the first $s$ non-critical special values of the Dirichlet $L$-function associated with $χ$ at least $c\sqrt{\frac{s}{\log s}}$ are irrational, where $c$ is a constant independent of $s$. This is a substantial improvement on work of Fischler when $4$ divides the conductor of $χ$. Otherwise, our constant improves on work of Mistiaen. The proof adapts some techniques of Lai and Yu for odd zeta values to the case of $L$-functions. The lack of positivity arguments is overcome by applying an irrationality criterion by Lai and Sprang originating from the $p$-adic setting.

title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
summary: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines. We also extend the Gaussent-Littelmann stratification to the parabolic setting, prove the Levi branching rule for LS galleries, and compare the resulting gallery model with Haines' maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks in the parabolic setting.

title: On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
summary: Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. These results were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

title: Relative homological algebra of filter modules
summary: Over an arbitrary ordered set we consider the class of filter modules, i.e. indicator modules of filters in the ordered set. We show that the induced exact structure of filter modules, the so-called filter exact structure, which has filter modules as relative projective modules, admits an explicit projectivization by the distributive lattice of filters. This allows the reduction of the projective-homological properties of the induced exact structure to the standard homological algebra of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$, the incidence algebra of $k$-representations on the lattice of filters. In the case of finite join-semilattices, we leverage the combinatorial structure of the distributive lattice of filters to determine the standard global dimension of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$. By virtue of projectivization we provide lower and upper bounds for the global dimension of the filter exact structure. Moreover, we call an ordered set filter-tiny if its relative injective modules one-to-one-correspond to the standard injective modules. We exploit relative derived functors to show that filter-tiny ordered sets do not admit relative injective prehulls if the relative global dimension is larger than 1. It is open to which classes of ordered sets $Q$ the filter-tininess condition applies, and what the relative injective modules are in the case of non-filter-tiny ordered sets.

title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
summary: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Thélène, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

title: Kloosterman Sums and Plücker Height Zeta Functions
summary: We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.

title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
summary: We prove that the shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$, $1\le j\le n$, are jointly universal for any nonzero real parameters $d_j$ with pairwise distinct absolute values. These restrictions are best possible. As an immediate consequence, we obtain generalized strong recurrence for arbitrary finite families of nonzero real parameters. Our proof uses Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem and a new variant of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem.

title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
summary: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

title: Estimates of Lucas series and expansions in non-integer bases
summary: Special Fibonacci and Lucas type expansions proved useful to ``correct'' some theorems on the number of expansions in non-integer bases \cite{BaiKomLor2021, KomLorPed2024, KomLorPed2025}. The proof of a key lemma was non-constructive. It was made constructive in the Fibonacci case by giving a precise estimate of the growth of the partial sums of the series of the inverses of the Fibonacci numbers \cite{KomPed2025}. In this paper we extend this result to the general case.

title: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
summary: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields.

title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
summary: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
summary:
We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n ρ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, where $ρ(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $φ$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $Γ\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
  Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $Γ$. Ordering the orbit $Γ\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\inΓ\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $φ$. Previously this was known either when $Γ=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $φ$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form.
  This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}λ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}χ(n)e^{2πi n^2 x}/n^s$.

title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
summary: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

title: On the Iwasawa invariants of admissible quadratic twists of elliptic curves at ordinary Eisenstein primes
summary: We study the Iwasawa $μ$- and $λ$-invariants of quadratic twists of rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes $p\geq 3$. We verify Greenberg's $μ=0$ conjecture for all such twists, which gives an Euler system free proof of Mazur's cotorsion conjecture, and study the $λ$-invariants when the twist is admissible in the sense of [GV00]. As a consequence, we prove the cyclotomic Iwasawa Main Conjecture and obtain the $p$-part BSD formulae in rank $0$ for admissible twists under mild conditions, covering many elliptic curves of potentially ordinary reduction.
